newsitem.title: CHINA: China corn official says no plan to end export ban.
newsitem.headline: China corn official says no plan to end export ban.

text.p: An official of China's National Maize Export Co on Thursday dismissed reports that Beijing was preparing to lift a ban on corn exports.
A Washington-based, private agricultural information service reported on Wednesday that China could be about to lift the ban, in force since late 1994.
"China does not allow exports of corn," said an official of the maize export company, which is run by the state-run China National Cereals, Oils and Foodstuffs Import and Export Corp.

Asked if China was planning to end the ban on corn exports, the official said: "There is no such thing. People have been saying this for a year, but we don't know where (this idea) is coming from," he said.
Top U.S. Agricultural Department officials said on Wednesday they had no confirmation that China was considering easing its export ban, but said they were investigating the reports.

Agricultural information service World Perspectives executive vice president Bob Kohlmeyer said reports from China suggested the northeastern province of Jilin could be permitted to export corn. He gave no details.
Jilin was recently permitted to ship 2.0 million tonnes to southern regions of China.

Chinese officials have been adamant that the ban, imposed in late 1994 when central reserves ran low, has not been lifted. China in the last few years has switched from being a major corn exporter to being an importer of U.S. corn.
